## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — REQ-7, AC-8 + decomposition PR 8.

## Surface
- CI gate: `cargo +nightly miri test -p polaris-backend --test tpm_signing` runs and passes.
- Code audit: confirms zero `unsafe` blocks in `polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/tpm/`. If any are required, each has a `// SAFETY:` justification AND a miri exercise.
- Add the miri job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as a non-blocking-yet-CI-visible step initially; promote to blocking once consistently green.

## Rust-quality notes
- Per rust-quality §5: this is the canonical unsafe-discipline closure. miri catches UB at runtime; the audit catches policy violations at review time.
- The miri job is slower than regular tests (often 10-100x). Mark it as a separate workflow job, not part of every PR's required-tests set initially.
- Document the unsafe-audit policy in the repo: "no hand-written `unsafe` in polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/tpm/; FFI lives inside tss-esapi; exceptions require explicit code review approval + miri exercise."

## External references
- miri docs: https://github.com/rust-lang/miri
- nightly toolchain pinning in CI: https://github.com/actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain

## Acceptance (AC-8)
- [ ] `cargo +nightly miri test -p polaris-backend --test tpm_signing` passes locally + in CI.
- [ ] Code audit confirms zero hand-written `unsafe` in the tpm module tree.
- [ ] Policy documented in `docs/dev/unsafe-discipline.md` (new file or extend existing).
